verdict.rationale: Yubico ships an official CLI, ykman (YubiKey Manager), documented as the way to "configure your YubiKey via the command line." A runtime probe confirms it installs from public registries and covers scriptable management of applications, PINs, PIV/OATH/OTP slots and device info. The firmware docs separately name ykman as a way to read device state. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party command documentation for each listed operation (enabling applications, setting PINs, managing slots) in the evidence, and hands-on runs of those operations rather than just the version check.

support.subject: As a developer, I can configure and manage the key from an official CLI — enable applications, set PINs, manage slots, read device state — scriptably

citations.quote: Configure your YubiKey via the command line.
Full scriptable device management: enable applications, PINs, PIV/OATH/OTP slots, device info.
The quickest and most convenient way to determine your device's firmware version is to use either the Yubico Authenticator ... or ykman
